engine.summary: Statistical process control and quality analytics: variables and attributes control charts with run tests, CUSUM and EWMA, process capability (normal, percentile and Box-Cox), gage R&R, hypothesis tests, correlation and regression, distribution fitting, Weibull reliability, event-time trend tests, changepoint detection, counter increments and time-series period and anomaly scoring.

surfaces.name: u-analytics
surfaces.error_shape: Err(...) of the module's error type, or None where a statistic is undefined for the data.

surfaces.name: @iyulab/u-analytics
surfaces.note: Native JS values in and out, typed in the .d.ts; an absent value in a result is null. Bundler and Node targets; no bundler-less browser build.
surfaces.error_shape: A thrown Error whose code property is the code, with the fields (parameter, index, min, max, exclusive_min, got, expected, ...) as its other properties.

surfaces.name: UAnalytics
surfaces.note: C ABI wrapper over the same wire layer; versioned on its own axis.
surfaces.error_shape: An AnalyticsException whose ErrorCode is the code, Parameter and Index the fields of those names, and Details the rest.

errors.shape: A refusal carries a stable snake_case 'code' and the fields listed for that code; how it arrives depends on the surface (error_shape).

source.catalog: code_catalog in src/wire.rs, built from the code table the refusals are made from; published as codes() in WebAssembly, over the C ABI and as Codes on .NET. What each code means is tabled in README.md, which a test holds equal to the catalog.

operations.summary: An X-bar R chart of subgroups: centre lines and 3-sigma limits of the means and ranges, the short-term sigma (R-bar / d2), each point's violations and whether the process is in control. Run tests: the 3-sigma test alone unless options.rules names a set (western_electric, nelson) or lists tests.

An X-bar S chart of subgroups: limits of the means and standard deviations, the short-term sigma (S-bar / c4), each point's violations and whether the process is in control. Run tests: the 3-sigma test alone unless options.rules names a set (western_electric, nelson) or lists tests.

An individuals and moving range chart of single values: limits of the values and moving ranges, each point's violations and whether the process is in control. Run tests: the 3-sigma test alone unless options.rules names a set (western_electric, nelson) or lists tests.
The run tests a series breaks against control limits the caller supplies, point by point. Run tests: the 3-sigma test alone unless options.rules names a set (western_electric, nelson) or lists tests.
A P chart of (defectives, sample size) pairs: the proportion defective with limits per sample size, from the data or a Phase I p-bar.
A Laney P' chart of (defectives, sample size) pairs: P chart limits widened by the overdispersion factor phi, from the data or a Phase I p-bar and phi.
A U chart of (defects, units) pairs: defects per unit with limits per quantity inspected, from the data or a Phase I u-bar.
A Laney U' chart of (defects, units) pairs: U chart limits widened by the overdispersion factor phi, from the data or a Phase I u-bar and phi.
An NP chart: the count of defectives in samples of one size, with fixed limits.
A C chart: the count of defects per inspection unit of one size, with fixed limits.
A G chart for rare events: limits on the conforming counts between events.
A T chart for rare events: limits on the times between events.
Process capability indices Cp, Cpk, Pp, Ppk and Cpm of a sample against specification limits, with the within-subgroup sigma given or estimated.
The Anderson-Darling test of normality: the statistic and its p-value.
The augmented Dickey-Fuller unit-root test of a series (no constant, constant, or constant and trend): the statistic, the lags and observations used, and critical values.
The Pearson, Spearman or Kendall (tau-b) correlation matrix of two or more variables of equal length, at least 3 values each.
Simple linear regression of y on x: slope, intercept, R^2, their standard errors, t and p values, the F test, fitted values and residuals; a statistic with no finite value (an exact fit) is null.

Every continuous family that fits the data by maximum likelihood, best AIC first, with parameters, log-likelihood, AIC and BIC: normal always; exponential, gamma, lognormal and Weibull for positive data; beta for data inside (0, 1).
The one-sample t test of mean = mu0: statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value.
Welch's two-sample t test (unequal variances): statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value.
The paired t test on y - x: statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value.
The Mann-Whitney U test by the normal approximation with tie correction.
The Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired samples; pairs with x = y are dropped.
The chi-squared goodness-of-fit test of observed counts against expected frequencies.
The Jarque-Bera test of normality (Jarque & Bera 1987 moment ratios).
The Shapiro-Wilk test of normality by Royston (1995), for 3 to 5000 values: W and its p-value.
The Mann-Kendall trend test with Kendall's tau and Sen's slope.

How much a cumulative counter advanced between neighbouring readings, each increment classified as normal, a declared reset, a wrap at a known modulus, or unexplained -- nothing about a fall is assumed.
A cumulative counter's increments summed over the intervals between edges, with the number of pairs in each and how many of them are unexplained.
The Laplace test of event times (a repairable system's failures) against a constant rate, for time- or failure-truncated observation: statistic, p-value and direction.
The MIL-HDBK-189 test of event times against a constant rate: chi^2 = 2 sum ln(T/t_i) with 2m degrees of freedom, p-value and direction.
The power-law process (Crow-AMSAA) fit of event times: beta and its unbiased estimate, lambda and the failure intensity at the end of observation.
One-way ANOVA across two or more groups: sums of squares, degrees of freedom, F and p-value.
The Kruskal-Wallis H test across two or more groups.
Levene's test for equal variances across groups, median-centred (Brown-Forsythe).
Bartlett's test for equal variances across groups.
The chi-squared test of independence on a contingency table of at least 2 x 2.
Fisher's exact test on a 2 x 2 table of whole counts.
Bonferroni-adjusted p-values, min(p m, 1), in input order.
Benjamini-Hochberg (1995) false-discovery-rate adjusted p-values, in input order.
Changepoints of a series by PELT (Killick et al. 2012) with an L2 or normal cost and a BIC or numeric penalty: the change positions and the number of segments.
Changepoints shared by several aligned signals by PELT over their summed cost.
Gage R&R by the average and range method: repeatability, reproducibility, part variation, %study variation, the number of distinct categories and the method's range and average chart limits.
Gage R&R by two-factor crossed ANOVA: the ANOVA table, variance components, %study variation and the number of distinct categories.
Percentile-based capability of non-normal data (ISO 22514-2): a fitted distribution's lower and upper percentiles and median against the specification limits, as Cp*, Cpk*, Cpl* and Cpu*.
A tabular CUSUM chart (Page 1954) for small persistent shifts in the mean: the upper and lower sums at each point, the decision interval h and the points that signal.
An EWMA chart (Roberts 1959): the exponentially weighted moving average with its time-varying limits and the points that signal.
Process capability of non-normal data through a Box-Cox transformation: the lambda used (estimated or given, and whether the estimate hit the search bound) and the indices on the transformed scale.
The dominant period of a univariate series by AutoPeriod: periodogram peaks confirmed on the autocorrelation function; null when no period passes.
An anomaly score for every point of a series by spectral residual saliency (Ren et al. 2019), with the expected value and band at each point and the points judged anomalous.
A sigma quality level as a defect rate in parts per million, by the Motorola convention with the 1.5-sigma shift: 10^6 (1 - Phi(sigma - 1.5)).
A defect rate in parts per million as a sigma quality level, the inverse of sigma_to_ppm (1.5-sigma shift included).

The maximum-likelihood Weibull fit of failure times with optional suspensions (right-censored times): shape, scale, log-likelihood and confidence intervals (Wald or likelihood ratio), with B-lives for given fractions failed.
The median-rank-regression Weibull fit (Bernard's ranks; Johnson's adjusted ranks with suspensions): shape, scale and R^2.
Reliability of a Weibull distribution: MTBF, and at given times the reliability R(t) and hazard rate h(t), and for given fractions failed the B-life.
